analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patch and metadata units against the indexed threat model and selected detailed evidence. CoordinatorClient.swift:120–141 adds an injectable reconnect policy; CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift:12–46 replaces exponential backoff with a randomized policy range based on session duration and close code. CoordinatorClientState.swift:509–537 adds a lock-protected recorder shared by the actor and transport callback. Connection.swift:185–186 measures duration after registration, not after authorization. Close-code capture at 418–421 precedes receive-error propagation; the parser at 513–521 bounds-checks the two-byte payload and exposes only a numeric code. No concrete disclosure or authorization regression is established by these changes.

Relevant contracts are availability (A-018, TB-002), connection-bound authorization and resumption (A-016, TB-011, T-053), cancellation (T-010), and fail-closed response encryption (T-008). Visible teardown still clears the socket nonce, registration/capacity state and chunk sink (Connection.swift:108–130), while receive handling checks connection identity before dispatch (385, 433). The changed code does not modify prompt encryption, cache isolation, billing, build qualification or privileged-helper controls; unchanged downstream implementations were not reviewed.

Integration must inspect CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorSessionEnd, absent here: validate finite, nonnegative, ordered and bounded delay ranges; escalation during repeated short sessions; reset criteria; and close-code-specific retry behavior. Verify that duration measured before authorization does not incorrectly classify repeated rejected registrations as healthy sessions. These missing policy details materially limit the availability conclusion but do not themselves prove a defect. Reconcile with other source passes and relevant tests; no finding is supported in this supplied scope.
